html:
Norilsk is a mining and smelting city above the Arctic Circle in northern Siberia, founded in 1935 and built by prisoners of the Gulag. It is the northernmost city in the world with more than 50,000 people, and no road or railway links it to the rest of Russia.

It sits on one of the richest bodies of nickel, copper and platinum ore on Earth. Norillag, the labour camp set up to build the mines and plants, held hundreds of thousands of prisoners over its life, and many thousands died of cold, hunger and overwork. In 1953, after Stalin's death, prisoners rose in the Norilsk uprising, one of the largest strikes in the camp system, before it was crushed.

Today the company Nornickel produces much of the world's nickel and palladium, used in steel, batteries and car exhaust filters. The smelters made Norilsk one of the most polluted places on Earth, with dead forest for miles around, and in 2020 a fuel tank burst and spilled about 20,000 tonnes of diesel into rivers. It is a closed city that foreigners need permission to visit. It marks the far end of the Russian conquest of Siberia.
